correctness.rationale: For each of n=13,14,15 the bundled morse_certificate.json specifies a permutation of all n pivot vertices. The verifier generates every independent triple of C_n^3 and every nonempty face of its complement-facet total-three-cut complex, then reconstructs each disjoint face/coface matching pair. Exact matching vectors are respectively 2716,6552,14400 pairs and critical vectors (one 0-cell plus one 5-cell), (one 0-cell plus one 6-cell), (one 0-cell plus two 8-cells). Directed Hasse incidences total 31070,84910,205800; a complete topological sort traverses all 5434,13106,28803 faces respectively, certifying acyclicity, not merely local compatibility. Forman discrete Morse theory produces one-point-based CW complexes with no other positive-dimensional cells, so all higher attaching maps target a point and the integral homotopy types are exactly S^5, S^6 and S^8 vee S^8. A separately implemented all-dimension GF(2) boundary reduction reproduces the predicted Betti vectors. Proof covers finite cases only; both executables and recorded outputs are embedded as independently checkable evidence.

originality.rationale: Carnero Bravo arxiv:2602.21427, Theorem 43(c), establishes the third-power d=3 one-sphere theorem only from 16 vertices onward, while Proposition 44 gives n=12. Question 49 explicitly asks for the gap 13<=n<=15, precisely the whole interval solved here. The full text was examined in its relevant sections. Bayer et al arxiv:2209.13503 treat squared cycles, not these third powers at d=3; their printed tables concern grid graph families. Chauhan-Shukla-Vinayak arxiv:2512.04486 classify total d=2 cases. These theorems do not imply the present three homotopy types, and none of the exact-parameter, equivalence and mathematical-record searches surfaced a dominating theorem. Bibliographic overlap remains possible.
residual_risks: No searched index can establish global priority or completeness of all unpublished/unindexed literature.
The comparison with the older foundational paper focused on its relevant sections and tables, not a proof that no implicit reformulation appears anywhere else.
The claims are finite-case results and do not solve the general three-parameter open question.

value.rationale: Question 49 of arxiv:2602.21427 defines a naturally bounded unsolved parameter window; at r=d=3 its entire first nonempty instance is exactly 13<=n<=15. The finding closes this interval with complete integral homotopy types, not a numerical or mod-two-only census. The endpoint n=15 contains two independent sphere summands and shows a structural transition between the known n=12 sphere and the n>=16 one-sphere regime. This exact boundary data is directly useful for understanding the general question; no arbitrary slice or general theorem is claimed.
